Prime example of the new rule: a static international treaty that is load-bearing for trade and industrial statistics and is cited on a recurring basis.

Contextual material from Banxico analysis (utilisation of T-MEC for exports to the United States):
Analyses repeatedly report the share of Mexican exports to the US that claim T-MEC preferential treatment (rising sharply in 2025 in response to higher non-USMCA tariffs). The agreement itself is the permanent legal framework; the statistical system measures compliance with and utilisation of its rules of origin and other disciplines. record.description: Framing of education access and learning outcomes. Foundational literacy and numeracy were already weak pre-crisis (very high learning poverty); subsequent disruption has further eroded proficiency and participation.
record._notes: Human-capital densification under severe stress.
record._url_evidence: World Bank Myanmar Monitoring Platform education page describing analysis of trends and disparities in educational outcomes, linking 'Educational Access and Learning Outcomes in Myanmar' and out-of-school children reports.
record._cadence_evidence: World Bank Myanmar education monitoring brief describes an ongoing study and monitoring effort, not a scheduled series. Only one dated output is shown (State of Education in Myanmar, July 2023) and no frequency is stated.

record.title: Natural hazard occurrence and impact statistics (typhoons, earthquakes, etc.)
record.publisher: NDRRMC / PSA related compilations
record.description: Compiled statistics on fatalities, injuries, affected population, damaged houses and economic losses from tropical cyclones, earthquakes and other natural hazards. Typhoons are the dominant recurring high-impact hazard.
record._notes: Core multi-hazard impact series. The Philippines lies on both the typhoon belt and the Pacific Ring of Fire.
record._url_evidence: Retrieved PSA 'Compendium of Philippine Environment Statistics 2015-2024, Component 4: Extreme Events and Disasters'. It compiles deaths, injured, missing, affected population and damaged houses (partially/totally) by hazard type - earthquakes, typhoons, floods, landslides - sourced from the Office of Civil Defense, with technical tables attached. ndrrmc.gov.ph still returns 403 to WebFetch.
record._url_route: publisher on-site product page via targeted search (psa.gov.ph environment statistics series)
record._cadence_evidence: The page states 'The Compendium of Philippine Environment Statistics is released annually'; this edition (Component 4, Extreme Events and Disasters, covering 2015-2024) was released 10 July 2025.

record.title: Life expectancy and health outcome statistics
record.publisher: WHO / national sources
record.description: Life expectancy at birth and related health indicators. Life expectancy is in the mid-to-high 70s; non-communicable diseases dominate the mortality profile.
record._notes: Core health-outcome densification.
record._url_evidence: Fetched WHO Data country page for Saudi Arabia showing 'Life expectancy at birth' and 'Leading causes of death, Saudi Arabia' sections.
record._cadence_evidence: data.who.int country overview for Saudi Arabia is a live interactive data portal; indicators carry mixed data years (2018-2023) and the only date given is an access date ('Accessed on 14 August 2026'), with no stated release cycle.
record.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

record.title: Greenhouse gas emissions statistics
record.publisher: Derived from international compilations
record.description: National GHG emissions estimates. Energy and oil-related activities dominate the emissions profile; the series is referenced in climate policy, NDC and energy-transition discussions under Vision 2030.
record._notes: Core climate-measurement node under oil dominance.
record._url_evidence: Fetched UNFCCC greenhouse gas profile for Saudi Arabia showing total GHG emissions for 1990/2010/2012 by gas and sector.

record.title: Internal displacement and return statistics
record.publisher: Derived from OCHA / UNHCR and monitoring sources
record.description: Statistics on internal displacement and returns. An estimated 5.5 million IDPs remain displaced; returns have accelerated in some periods but large residual displacement persists. Continuously cited in every humanitarian and demographic assessment.
record._notes: Highest-centrality humanitarian and demographic-stress node.
record._url_evidence: OCHA's Syrian Arab Republic country page, stating some 7 million people internally displaced, over 4 million refugees, and around 1.9 million IDPs plus 900,000 refugees returned since December.
record._cadence_evidence: OCHA Syria country page is a funding/needs landing hub. The only publication on it is an undated 'Briefing to the Security Council on the humanitarian situation in Syria'; there is no situation-report list, no flash-update cadence and no stated release frequency.

record.title: Wheat production and food-security statistics
record.publisher: Derived from national and monitoring sources
record.description: Statistics on wheat production. Output collapsed during conflict and drought years; recent seasons show recovery toward multi-million-ton levels in favourable rainfall years. Eastern governorates remain the main production base. Food security remains fragile.
record._notes: Core food-security crop densification under recovery conditions.
record._url_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for the Syrian Arab Republic (23 February 2026), giving 2025 cereal production of 1.2 million tonnes (over 60 percent below average) and 2025/26 wheat import requirements of 3 million tonnes.
record._cadence_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Syria shows 'Reference Date: 23-February-2026' and a current-issue PDF, plus an archive of Special Reports (1999, 2012, 2013, 2015-2019, 2021) and GIEWS Updates (2012, 2014, 2020) that is plainly irregular. The page states no update frequency for the country brief itself.

record.title: Education disruption and out-of-school statistics
record.publisher: Derived from UNICEF and education monitoring sources
record.description: Statistics and framing of education access under conflict and recovery. Approximately 2.45 million children are out of school; thousands of schools remain non-functional. Continuously cited in humanitarian and human-capital analysis.
record._notes: Core education densification under severe conflict disruption.
record._url_evidence: UNICEF Syria education programme page, stating about 2 million children out of school and over 7,000 schools damaged or destroyed.
record._cadence_evidence: UNICEF Syria education page is an evergreen thematic programme page, not a dated publication. Its Resources block links 'Response snapshots' covering 2025-2026 periods (e.g. 'January to December 2025') but the page states no publication schedule.

record.title: Health access and nutrition statistics
record.publisher: Derived from UNICEF / WHO and humanitarian sources
record.description: Statistics on health-service access and malnutrition. Large shares of the population require nutrition support; hundreds of thousands of children under five are affected by life-threatening malnutrition. Health-system functionality remains severely constrained.
record._notes: Core health and nutrition densification under humanitarian emergency conditions.
record._url_evidence: WHO EMRO Syrian Arab Republic country page, showing the country health indicator set (population, maternal mortality ratio, primary health care centres per 10,000, life expectancy, health expenditure) and health-sector situation reports.
record._cadence_evidence: WHO EMRO Syria country page is an institutional landing page. It alludes to 'Situation reports on north-west Syria' and health-sector 4Ws snapshots but gives no cadence; the newest dated items are news stories from 21 January 2020 and 17 December 2019, and the framework document is dated 2018.

record.title: Electricity generation and capacity statistics
record.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Electricity and monitoring sources
record.description: Statistics on electricity production and available capacity. Generation remains far below pre-war levels; chronic shortfalls, fuel constraints and damaged infrastructure are structural features. Limited renewable contribution is emerging.
record._notes: Core power-system statistical product under severe infrastructure damage.

record.title: Fiscal balance and revenue statistics
record.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Finance and IMF-aligned monitoring
record.description: Fiscal revenue, expenditure and balance indicators under transitional conditions. Recent readings show very constrained absolute revenues and spending relative to pre-war levels; customs and limited hydrocarbon receipts feature among available sources. Budget planning remains highly constrained.
record._notes: Core fiscal-flow node under extreme revenue and institutional constraints.
record._url_evidence: Central Bank of Syria 'إحصاءات مالية' (Financial Statistics) category page covering government accounts indicators, estimated budget resources, expenditures and executed budget operations, including the overall balance to GDP ratio; the Ministry of Finance site (syrianfinance.gov.sy, mof.gov.sy) is unreachable via WebFetch.
record._cadence_evidence: CBS government-finance landing page lists only table headings (key indicators of government accounts, estimated budget resources, estimated budget payments, executed budget operations). No dates, editions or periodicity are shown. The site's periodic series named elsewhere (weekly economic report, monthly inflation report, annual business report) are not tied to this fiscal page.

record.title: Syria–Turkey merchandise trade statistics
record.publisher: Derived from Turkish and Syrian trade monitoring sources
record.description: Bilateral trade with Turkey. Volumes have risen in the post-transition period; Turkey is a major source of imports and a key overland trade corridor. Multiple border crossings are active; trade growth is a leading indicator of external re-engagement.
record._notes: Primary regional bilateral trade densification under recovery conditions.

record.title: Drought and agricultural water-stress statistics
record.publisher: Derived from FEWS NET and climate monitoring sources
record.description: Statistics and framing of drought conditions and water stress. Consecutive drought years have sharply reduced rainfed cereal output and groundwater; recent improved rainfall has supported recovery but cumulative damage to water resources and productive assets persists.
record._notes: High-centrality environmental constraint node linking agriculture and food security.
record._url_evidence: FEWS NET Syria country page carrying the Food Security Outlook and Key Message Updates (June 2026 - January 2027), analysing drought, water scarcity and agricultural constraints with IPC phase classifications.
record._cadence_evidence: FEWS NET Syria page lists a rotating set of dated products - Food Security Outlook (June 2026 - January 2027), Food Security Outlook Update (April - September 2026) and a single-month Key Message Update (July 2026) - i.e. one dated analysis per month across the three product types. The page states no frequency in words and no countable archive is exposed, so 12 is read off the monthly-dated product rotation.

record.title: Poverty and living standards statistics
record.publisher: NSO / NESDC related / World Bank-aligned
record.description: Official and compiled poverty rates and living-standards indicators. National poverty has declined to low single digits on some measures; upper-middle-income poverty lines still show residual double-digit shares, with regional disparities.
record._notes: Core welfare measurement node.
record._url_evidence: NSO household income/expenditure indicator branch listing the poverty line, poverty incidence and number of poor, sourced from NESDC.
record._cadence_evidence: NSO statistics branch 309 (household income and expenditure) lists ten series - household income, expenditure, debt, poverty line, share and number of poor, Gini coefficients - each as annual observations, with coverage 2547-2566 and 2555-2566 and dissemination dates of 10 October 2567 and 25 December 2568. Annual counted from the yearly data points; no periodicity is stated in words.

record.title: Defence and security expenditure statistics
record.publisher: Ministry of National Defence / Ministry of Treasury and Finance / SIPRI-aligned
record.description: Official and compiled statistics on defence and security spending. Recent budgets place total defence and security expenditure in the mid-to-high USD 20 billions range (roughly 2.3% of GDP in 2026 projections), with further planned increases. Includes Ministry of National Defence and related security allocations.
record._notes: Core defence-resource node. Rising nominal and real commitments under inflation and strategic pressures.
record._url_evidence: NATO 'Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014-2025)' report containing Türkiye's series in current-price liras (1,361,307 mn in 2025) and defence spending as a share of GDP (2.33% estimated for 2025); msb.gov.tr is unreachable via WebFetch.

record.title: Vietnam–United States merchandise trade statistics
record.publisher: GSO / customs / derived bilateral compilations
record.description: Bilateral goods trade with the United States. The US is Vietnam’s largest single export market; key categories include electronics/telephones, computers, furniture, apparel and footwear. Trade volumes have expanded rapidly over the past decade.
record._notes: High-centrality bilateral trade node. USA is the dominant export destination.
record._url_evidence: National Statistics Office release page whose data tables include 'Imports and exports by country group, country and territory' (the official bilateral goods-trade series); no US-only page exists on the NSO site.
record._cadence_evidence: NSO page is headed 'Preliminary data tables of months in 2025 about Exports of goods, Imports of goods' - one export/import value table per month.

record.title: National logistics and multimodal connectivity framing
record.publisher: Derived from maritime, transport and planning sources
record.description: Policy and analytical framing of Vietnam’s logistics system — seaports, inland connectivity, and the role of logistics in supporting manufacturing exports and FDI. Continuously referenced in trade-facilitation and competitiveness discussions.
record._notes: System-level logistics framing node.
_referenced_by: Seaport throughput and major port nodes
record._url_evidence: MOIT's official logistics portal page for the Vietnam Logistics Report 2023, the recurring national logistics report (seven chapters on infrastructure, services, regional logistics).
record._cadence_evidence: Page states that since 2017 the Ministry of Industry and Trade produces the 'Bao cao Logistics Viet Nam thuong nien' (annual Vietnam Logistics Report); this is the 2023 edition.

record.title: Ethnic minority poverty and living-standards statistics
record.publisher: GSO / World Bank-aligned and national poverty monitoring
record.description: Poverty rates and living-standards indicators disaggregated by ethnicity. Ethnic minorities account for a large majority of remaining poverty despite representing a minority of the population; absolute numbers of poor ethnic minorities have fallen substantially over the past decade.
record._notes: Core equity / residual-poverty densification.

record.title: Oil production and export statistics
record.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Oil and IMF-aligned sources
record.description: Statistics on crude oil production and exports. Production has collapsed from pre-war peaks near 400+ thousand barrels per day to the low tens of thousands (or lower) in recent years; export interruption has been a central fiscal and external shock.
record._notes: Core (collapsed) extractive node. Highest pre-war centrality; now a defining absence.
record._url_evidence: IEA Yemen oil country statistics page (breadcrumb Yemen/Middle East, oil supply/production/trade section); figures are rendered client-side so no numbers appear in the fetched text. Yemen's own Ministry of Oil domains (mom.gov.ye, moom.gov.ye) are unreachable via WebFetch.
record._cadence_evidence: IEA Yemen oil country page carries only explanatory narrative about oil supply and refining; no last-updated date, data vintage, source dataset or update-frequency note appears anywhere on it.

record.description: Statistics on food insecurity and humanitarian needs. Inadequate food consumption affects a majority of the population in recent monitoring; severe deprivation and reliance on crisis coping strategies are widespread across both control areas.

record.title: Internal displacement statistics
record.publisher: Derived from IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix and OCHA sources
record.description: Statistics on internal displacement. Yemen hosts one of the world’s largest IDP populations; new displacement continues even in periods of relative de-escalation, with Ma’rib and other governorates as major destinations.
record._notes: High-centrality humanitarian and demographic-stress node.
record._url_evidence: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix Yemen country page listing Rapid Displacement Tracking, Area Assessment, Flow Monitoring Registry and MCLA products plus the Annual DTM Displacement Report and National Displacement Profile.
record._cadence_evidence: IOM DTM Yemen page's flagship product is the Rapid Displacement Tracking (RDT) update, published weekly (alongside monthly Flow Monitoring Registry, quarterly Area Assessments and an annual report); 60+ dated products listed, most recent shown July 2024.

record.title: Agriculture production statistics
record.publisher: Derived from national and USDA/FAO-aligned sources
record.description: Statistics on crop production. Sorghum, millet, wheat and other cereals are produced at low absolute levels relative to national food needs; Yemen is heavily import-dependent for staple cereals. Agriculture remains important for rural livelihoods under severe water and conflict constraints.
record._notes: Core primary-sector production node under import dependence and conflict stress.
record._url_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Yemen (dated June 2026) giving 2025 cereal production of about 400,000 tonnes, wheat and sorghum crop notes, and 2026 cereal import requirements of 5.2 million tonnes.
record._cadence_evidence: FAO GIEWS Country Brief for Yemen, current issue reference date 04-June-2026; the linked PDF archive (YEM_Archive.pdf) lists ~16 dated editions across 2015-2025, i.e. roughly one to three per year, averaging about 1.5.

record.title: Fiscal balance and revenue statistics
record.publisher: Derived from IMF-aligned and national fiscal monitoring
record.description: Fiscal revenue, expenditure and balance indicators. Government revenues (excluding grants) have collapsed relative to pre-war levels; deficits are financed under extreme constraint with heavy reliance on grants and limited domestic sources. Dual control further fragments fiscal capacity.
record._notes: Core fiscal-flow node under extreme revenue collapse and dual institutions.
record._url_evidence: Central Bank of Yemen annual report series page; the 2024 report contains Chapter Three 'المالية العامة' (Public Finance) alongside the external sector chapter, the only regularly published official fiscal accounts. Covers IRG-controlled fiscal space only.
record._cadence_evidence: Same CBY page as the BOP item (pages/31): the Annual Reports series, one edition per year (2020, 2022-2025), which is where the fiscal/external tables sit.
